metaTitle: Point and Click Museum · A History of Adventure Games
metaDescription: An interactive pixel art museum about the history of adventure games: from Colossal Cave and Zork to Monkey Island and today's releases. Timeline, studios, engines, techniques, minigames and DOSBox in your browser.
metaKeywords: adventure games, point and click, history, LucasArts, Sierra, SCUMM, Monkey Island, pixel art, DOSBox, retro games
ogImageAlt: Pixel art façade of the Point and Click Museum at night
soundTitle: Turn sound effects on or off
crtTitle: Turn the CRT monitor filter on or off
noscript: Turn on JavaScript to play the minigames. All the museum content can still be read.
subtitle: A HISTORY OF THE ADVENTURE GAME · 1976 – TODAY
tagline: A museum you explore with the mouse: verbs, inventories, impossible puzzles and almost fifty years of stories.
heroCanvasLabel: Pixel art façade of the museum. Tap the moon, the street lamp, the sign, the door, the cat or the arcade cabinet.
heroHint: Tap the façade. Some things react.
introRoom: From the two-word parsers of 1976 to today's indie adventures: almost fifty years of puzzles, impossible inventories and dialogue choices.
introVisit: Every discovery scores points, as in Sierra's adventures. There are 100.
introPlay: Four minigames and an arcade room of MS-DOS adventures.
timelineLead: Half a century of adventures, era by era.
studiosLead: The museum guide knows them all. Pick a studio and ask away: conversations work like a dialogue tree.
byeAnswer: Any time. The other rooms are waiting.
enginesLead: Every great studio had its own tool. Insert a cartridge into the console to read its spec sheet.
techniquesLead: The tricks that made the genre possible.
parallaxHint: Move your mouse or finger over the scene
musicQueued: Change queued: it will kick in at the start of the next bar...
musicSwitched: Switched at the start of the bar. Current theme: {theme}.
soundOff: Sound is off: turn it on in the top bar to hear it.
ideasTitle: Design ideas that changed the genre
arcadeIdle: Pick an adventure from the list or load your own copy.

fullscreenFail: This viewer doesn't allow full screen.
byoBody: Open a .zip or .jsdos of a game you own, for MS-DOS or ScummVM. It never leaves your computer.
byoExe: Executable inside the .zip (DOS games only; leave empty to detect it)
byoNoExe: Enter the executable, for example GAME.EXE or GAME\START.BAT.
footer: A non-profit tribute to graphic adventures. Box art, screenshots and logos belong to their owners.
certBody: You have earned all 100 points of the Point and Click Museum. The guide hands you a golden key and a mug of grog... well, cocoa. Thanks for visiting.
langHintText: This page is also available in English.
mapLead: Six rooms and four minigames, in any order you like.
gamesLead: Four games. They all score points.
enginesListTitle: See all engines as a list
mouseModeTitle: Switch between capturing the mouse (recommended for DOS games) and direct mode
mouseHintLock: Click the game screen to capture the mouse. Press Esc to release it.
mouseHintDirect: Direct mode: the game pointer follows the browser pointer. Use it when capture isn't available.
pointerLockFail: This browser won't let the page capture the mouse here: switched to direct mode.
page_timeline_meta: The most important adventure games from 1976 to today, by era: from Colossal Cave and Zork to Monkey Island, Grim Fandango and Return to Monkey Island.
page_studios_meta: Infocom, Sierra, LucasArts, Revolution, Pendulo, Telltale, Wadjet Eye and other studios that shaped the adventure game, told through a dialogue tree.
page_engines_meta: Z-machine, AGI, SCUMM, SCI, Virtual Theatre, AGS, GrimE, ScummVM and today's engines: the tools behind every adventure.
page_techniques_meta: Colour cycling, dithering, parallax, iMUSE dynamic music and the evolution of the verb interface, with interactive demos.
page_games_meta: Four original adventure minigames: text adventure, verb room, pixel hunt and timeline challenge.
page_text-adventure_meta: A text adventure you can play in the browser: type commands and find the lost floppy.
page_restoration-room_meta: A point and click adventure with verbs and inventory: escape the museum's restoration room.
page_pixel-hunt_meta: Find the golden floppy in an ever darker attic. A tribute to pixel hunting.
page_chronology_meta: Sort classic adventure games by release year.
page_arcade_meta: Classic MS-DOS and ScummVM adventures to play in the browser: freeware, demos and gems from the 80s and 90s.
